name: Red's Eats
season: late April/May to mid-October (2026: opened May 6, target closing Oct. 13)
founded_note: Disputed by a year: its About page says it has been at the foot of Wiscasset's Main Street for 88 years (2026) while its home page says 'Celebrating Red's Eats 87th year'; the Bangor Daily News called 2026 its 88th year in business. Named by Harold Delano, called 'Red'; the late Al Gagnon left it to his four children, who run it now.
note: Family-run takeout stand at the foot of Wiscasset's Main Street on Route 1, known for lobster rolls and long summer lines.

name: Five Islands Lobster Co.
season: summer into fall (2026: daily in August, then weekends only Sept. 11 to Oct. 11)
founded_note: Its site says current owners Keith and Gina Longbottom have run it since 2007.
note: Counter-service lobster shack on the working wharf in the fishing village of Five Islands, with picnic tables facing Sheepscot Bay; no alcohol sold, coolers welcome.

name: McLoons Lobster Shack
note: Lobster shack on Spruce Head Island across from a working lobster wharf, with island views; the menu changes daily with what is available.

name: Young's Lobster Pound
note: Lobster pound with picnic tables on the Passagassawakeag River in Belfast.

name: Sprague's Lobster
founded_note: Frank Sprague marked 50 seasons in business in 2025 (it began as a lobster-bake catering company). The Lincoln County News says the eatery has been at its Main Street spot for 37 of those years, and also that he moved to the Route 1 location and made it a restaurant 27 years ago; the figures don't agree.
note: Family-run lobster stand on the Creamery Pier in Wiscasset known for lobster rolls and lobster dinners.

name: Muscongus Bay Lobster
season: late May into fall (2025 season opened May 23)
note: Family-owned wholesale and retail lobster business on Round Pond Harbor with outdoor waterfront tables and a small beer-and-wine bar, the Bait Shed Bar.

name: Robinson's Wharf
founded_note: Its site says it was established over 40 years ago.
note: Waterfront seafood restaurant with a seafood market and gift shop just across the swing bridge from Boothbay Harbor; the market is open year-round.

name: Larson's Lunch Box
founded_note: Its page says the current owners (Tim and Tamara, who also own the Damariscotta River Grill) took over from retiring owners and that 2024 was their third season.
note: Outdoor takeout shack in a parking lot just north of downtown Damariscotta, serving lobster and crab rolls in season; its page says it will be back in spring 2026.

name: Moody's Diner
founded_note: Percy and Bertha Moody started the business in 1927 with cabins on the hill above old Route 1 and a lunch cart in 1929; when the current Route 1 opened in 1934 the cart was moved down to the new highway and grew into the diner at Route 1 and Route 220 (LCN 2017, Wikipedia). The family counts 1927 as its start (90th anniversary in 2017).
note: Family-run Route 1 diner known for its pies, baked from Bertha Moody's recipes, and its whoopie pies; open just about every day of the year.

name: Dorman's Dairy Dream
season: spring to fall (2026: opened April 9, Thursday–Sunday 12–7)
founded_note: Est. 1951 and 'celebrating 75 years' in 2026 (its site); sources don't say whether it has always been at this address.
note: Long-running roadside ice cream stand in Thomaston.

name: King Eider's Pub
dishes: Damariscotta River oysters on the half shell
founded_note: Its site says it has served Damariscotta since 1996; LCN (Nov. 2025) says the Elm Street pub has poured drinks since 1996.
note: English-style pub in downtown Damariscotta with a raw bar of Damariscotta River oysters and a whiskey list of 180-plus bottles.

name: Damariscotta River Grill
dishes: Pemaquid oysters (half shell, pan-roasted or fried)
note: Two-level restaurant and bar on Damariscotta's Main Street serving Pemaquid oysters from the river outside its windows; same owners as Larson's Lunch Box.

name: The Shuck Station
founded_note: Started as Brendan Parsons' oyster cart in Portland's Old Port before moving to Newcastle (its site).
note: Raw bar run by oyster farmer and competition shucker Brendan Parsons, serving Damariscotta River oysters including his own Blackstone Point oysters.

name: Mine Oyster
note: Waterfront raw bar and night club on Pier 1 run by chef Ralph Smith; it hosts the annual Pemaquid Oyster Festival with oysters from about 10 Damariscotta River farms (2025 and 2026).

name: Glidden Point Oyster Farms
founded_note: Ryan McPherson had owned the farm for roughly eight years as of January 2025 (LCN).
note: Damariscotta River oyster farm whose farm store serves its oysters seven days a week with local beer and wine, with a food truck on site in summer; farm tours too.

name: Jolie Rogers Raw Bar
note: Oyster bar by the Sheepscot River run by Andy Rogers and Ryan Jolie; Rogers won the Pemaquid Oyster Festival shucking contest three years running through 2026.

name: Sea Basket
note: Wiscasset seafood restaurant known for generous portions and lobster stew made with fresh local lobster meat.

name: Dunton's Doghouse
dishes: Riley Dog with cheese and bacon
note: Small hot dog stand at the edge of downtown Boothbay Harbor serving natural-casing dogs and W.A. Bean red hot dogs on griddled, buttered New England-style buns.

name: Harbor Dogs
founded_note: In business for more than 60 years (Press Herald, 2026); not stated whether always at this spot.
note: Seasonal hot dog stand in a parking lot at the edge of Camden Harbor, using Jordan's red snappers on toasted New England-style buns.

name: Taste of Maine
founded_note: Family owned and operated since 1978; open 48 years as of 2026 (BDN).
note: Landmark Route 1 seafood restaurant with a giant lobster on its roof and a dining room full of Maine antiques; sold in 2026, with new owners taking over in late August or September (owners said 'same crew, same menu').

name: Delano's Seafood Shack
founded_note: The shack opened in a trailer in winter 2020; its new building opened Dec. 3, 2025 (LCN).
note: Year-round seafood shack next to the Delano family's seafood market, run by former lobsterman Kendall Delano Jr.; moved from a trailer into a new building with indoor seating in late 2025.

name: Deb's Bristol Diner
note: Small diner in the center of Bristol on Route 130, run by Debbie Thibault.

name: Bray Brook Farm
note: Farm (with donkeys) and ice cream shop in Appleton with several unique hard-serve flavors.

name: Jefferson Scoop
note: Ice cream stand in the center of Jefferson scooping Gifford's ice cream and soft serve, plus smoothies and slushies.

name: John's Ice Cream Factory
founded_note: Says its ice cream tradition dates to the late 1800s, when the current owner's grandfather made desserts in Italy (its claim, via the Press Herald).
note: Family-owned ice cream shop in Liberty selling cones and take-home pints and quarts.
